newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures close up 17 cents, but below $18.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures close up 17 cents, but below $18.

text.p: IPE Brent futures for May closed at $17.93 on Tuesday, up 17 cents, but well below the day's high of $18.09.

The front month contract gained value in the morning on a technical bounce and pegged up above $18 after the NYMEX opened. But it failed to hold its strength and traded in a narrow range for much of the afternoon.

Some dealers were heartened at the pick-up after last week's heavy falls, with Friday's low of $17.65 never in danger of being tested and talk instead of upside resistance. Other players said business was choppy, thin and directionless.
Brokers said better prices for physical crude lent the market some support but all eyes will now be on American Petroleum Institute (API) stock figures due out later.
"The market needs some sort of direction and could get it from that," said one broker.
Forecasts differ for whether the API survey will show a crude build or draw in the well-supplied North American market.

"The market has been levelling out. Everything depends on the APIs. If there is a stock draw that will push us through the resistance level of $18.10 and give us easy access to $18.40," said one broker.
May Brent's high was $18.09 and the contract made several attempts to rally above the $18 level but slipped back each time. One trader said $18.10 proved stubbornly unbreachable today.
April gas oil, which expires on Thursday had earlier closed quietly at $163, up $1 on the day, but 50 cents off its high.
Brokers said business followed Monday's pattern, gaining with New York before trailing lower later.
"The gas oil market is trying to stabilise but it doesn't really have enough confidence in itself," said one broker.
